note: Checks whose result follows the speed of the machine that runs them. Each was calibrated on the maintainer's machine (Apple M2 Pro), where it passes and where release-cut.mjs enforces it in the staged run of every cut. GitHub's hosted runners are slower and run the three browsers side by side on 3 CPUs, and these checks have failed there on speed alone. With TYPESET_HOSTED_RUNNER=1 (set by ci.yml and the release workflow's verify job) verify-release.mjs reports a failing check listed here as SLOW, with its detail, and does not fail the run; everywhere else, and with --strict, it is enforced like any other check. An entry needs the runs that show it failing on speed; label is a regular expression over check labels, and browser narrows an entry.

entries.label: ^Typeset(Rich)?Text at 4x CPU: a cold screen push paints every on-screen block composed in its first frame$
entries.reason: The adapters compose on-screen blocks before the first paint unless that work exceeds VISIBLE_BUDGET_MS (120 ms), the engine's safety valve for a very slow device (src/lib/v4/adapter-registry.ts); a hosted runner at 4x CPU is that device.
entries.observed: macos-15 run 36258432379: TypesetText 13 of 16 on-screen blocks uncomposed in the first frame. ubuntu-latest run 36255458992: TypesetText 16 of 19, TypesetRichText 4 of 19. M2 Pro: 0.

entries.label: ^TypesetText in an overflow:auto scroller, scrolled in 0 ms after mounting: no block paints native lines and is rewrapped$
entries.reason: Whether the scroll lands before the visible blocks' first composition finishes is timing.
entries.observed: macos-15 run 36258432379: 1 flash frame (1 block) in 125 frames. M2 Pro: 0.

entries.label: : recomposes after updates with no audit error$
entries.reason: The audit samples each block 260 ms after the fifth update; on a hosted runner WebKit's first recomposition can take longer, so the sample catches it in progress (stale-layout, stale-output). Every later sample is clean.
